details:
Q1: Which guarded operations should stop using the 300-second PR cache?
Choices:
A) Remote writes only: Bash `git push` targets with `reaches_remote=True` and both MCP push tools (`_evaluate_mcp_push`) always query GitHub, once per (repo, branch) per hook call using the existing `pr_snapshots` map. Local `git commit` checks keep using the cache, since nothing strands until a push. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Every guarded operation, local commits included: remove cache reads entirely, keeping `_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS` / `_read_cache` / `_write_cache` defined for compatibility.
C) Keep the cache for remote writes but lower the TTL (for example to 30 seconds).
Q2: When a remote write cannot get fresh PR state (GitHub lookup fails), what should the hook do?
Choices:
A) Keep the existing §21.C behaviour in `_unreachable_outcome`: block when git history shows stranded work, otherwise ask for human confirmation. Never fall back to cached state. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Always deny the remote write (exit 2) when fresh state cannot be verified, as the issue suggests. This also changes the documented CLAUDE.md §21.C policy for pushes, which the fix would then need to update.
**Note:** B together with Q1:B would also hard-deny local commits whenever GitHub is unreachable, unless commits are explicitly exempted.
